correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the legal (k−1)-vertex overlap graph, with F_(k+2) required edges, strong connectivity via append-ones paths, and signs of out-minus-in imbalances from initial/final bits. The potential g(v) counts initial ones before first zero, setting g(1^(k−1))=k−2; verified every legal edge loses at most one. Summing g against imbalances gives S=F_k−1 and hence R>=S−(k−2)=F_k−k+1 even for arbitrary walk endpoints. The constructive augmentation duplicates j successive append-one edges for each negatively imbalanced vertex except 1^(k−2)0, bijectively balancing remaining positive vertices, with Euler trail from 01^(k−2) to 1^(k−2)0. Checked special k=2 Euler circuit. Inspected checker.py. Independent exact potential and Fibonacci counts recomputed k=2..8, and its own bounded BFS k<=5 is visibly exhaustive; the all-k proof is the potential+augmentation argument.
